criteria.criterion: Change the payload to an owning resource whose zero ID is valid. Derive an ownership-bearing tagged option and show why the old niche and byte-copy rules fail. Compare the exact documented Rust Option representation cases with this C design; no blanket ABI equivalence is allowed. Analyze void as an incomplete type with no values and _Noreturn as a function specifier. Compile a struct member of type void and an expression attempting to use a void result as a payload under strict C17 diagnostics; do not execute a falsely returning _Noreturn function. Construct a named one-state enum payload as a protocol-level unit and explain why it is not an uninhabited type or a general coercion rule.

criteria.demonstration: The late changed-condition owner stage actually imports PR-T66-09 memory.adversarial_allocator after T66, avoiding a reverse early prerequisite. Strict GCC/Clang diagnostics reject void members, void payload use and returning Noreturn bodies without executing them. A protocol unit enum is validated separately. Actual Rust1.93.1 moved-value rejection and single Drop demonstrate a narrower language comparison than C enforcement or ABI equivalence. All13cost dimensions, real allocation/release counts, seven scalar/owner timing samples and build/object/stack observations are retained; unlike contracts are not reported as overhead.

limits: Public C objects require well-formed tags, unique ownership, live allocator contexts and external serialization.
Actual allocator has bounded typed backing; accounting does not establish arbitrary allocator correctness.
Arm32 evidence is an object-layout observation only; no hosted Arm execution, link or physical claim.
Rust1.93.1 observations and rolling1.99.1 documentation are distinct; no blanket C/Rust ABI promise.
